output.diagnosis: BlueQuartz's vendor payments contact states in writing that this bill was already cleared in an earlier batch and that remittance advice went to an accounts email that may no longer be current, asking us to verify at our end. Separately, the payer notes record their AP head describing the bill as 'under query' and asking that all communication be routed through a single email id with SMS stopped. The ledger still shows an outstanding balance and the invoice is well past its due date, so the payer's claim and our records disagree and cannot be reconciled from this snapshot.
output.reasoning: An already-paid claim plus a stated internal query is not ordinary lateness. The remittance advice may have gone to a stale address on our side, so a human needs to check receipts against this reference before any further chase. Another automated reminder or a payment link would repeat the exact contact the payer has objected to and risks chasing a possibly settled bill. Payment history shows a payer who has consistently settled in full, though habitually past terms, which makes a clerical or channel mismatch a plausible explanation rather than avoidance. There is also an explicit channel preference to honour. I am not treating the payer's assertion as proof the balance is zero; the outstanding figure still stands in the record, which is precisely why a person should reconcile it. No promise-to-pay phrase appears in the prose.
